summary: Norbyte's BG3 Script Extender is a Windows-only DWrite.dll proxy that downloads a per-game-version DLL and bootstraps from 69 byte-pattern mappings in BinaryMappings.xml resolving 99 game symbols, using Microsoft Detours for hooks; Norbyte states directly (bg3se issue #539, 2025-11-13) that those MSVC patterns will not match the Linux binary because it is built with a different compiler, and there is no Linux port — issue #530 has sat open since the native build shipped. The WASD movement mod (Ch4nKyy/BG3WASD, open source) does NOT synthesise mouse clicks: it copies the CameraForward/Backward/Left/Right keybinds onto the CharacterMoveForward/Backward/Left/Right commands in inputremap_pN.json and then NOPs one controller-mode gate so the game's own analog-controller movement path accepts keyboard input — a data file plus one code patch. I verified this technique's anchors survive verbatim into our Linux ELF: CharacterMoveForward is still command 0x9d/157, and I located GetInputValue at 0x2d1d880 (58 call sites), the movement-vector reader at 0x2c75cd0 reading 0xa0/0x9f/0x9d/0x9e, HandleCameraInput at 0x2c82bf0 reading 0x66/0x65/0x64, and the sole SDL_PollEvent call site at 0x02e9e7c8. The only public native-Linux BG3 code mod is ahungry/bg3-linux-ae, a 299-line LD_PRELOAD .so doing mprotect+memcpy byte patches found by scanning /proc/self/maps — and all four of its historical byte patterns score ZERO hits in our binary (4.1.1.7398727), which is the strongest available argument for our symbol/reloc approach over pattern scanning. The closest architectural prior art is tdimino/bg3se-macos, a ground-up non-Windows SE rebuild whose PORTING.md says explicitly that having a symbol table makes re-porting "run a script and paste the output" instead of a multi-hour RE session.

key_addresses.what: GetInputValue(playerController, commandId, playerIdx) — the central input-read primitive that every BG3WASD hook targets on Windows
key_addresses.evidence: numpy scan of .text for e8 rel32 targeting it: 'call sites to 0x2d1d880: 58'. Called with esi=0x9d/0x9e/0x9f/0xa0 (movement) at 0x2c75ce4/cf8/d0c/d20 and with esi=0x66/0x65/0x64 (camera) at 0x2c82c05/c1d/c35. Matches BG3WASD doc/guide.md: 'These variables are then passed to a function I name GetInputValue. All 4 calls of this function are hooked by the mod!'

key_addresses.what: GetMovementInputVec / GetMovementInputWorldVec equivalent — reads all four movement axes and combines them into a vector
key_addresses.evidence: bg3q.py dis 0x2c75cd0: 'mov esi, 0xa0; call 0x2d1d880' then 0x9f, then 0x9d, then 0x9e, results merged via 'insertps xmm0, dword ptr [rsp + 0x14], 0xc' at 0x2c75d2a. This is the exact structure the Windows guide describes.

key_addresses.what: HandleCameraInput equivalent — the function BG3WASD's BlockCameraInputCavehook patches to stop the camera consuming WASD
key_addresses.evidence: bg3q.py dis 0x2c82bf0: 'mov esi, 0x66 / call 0x2d1d880', 'mov esi, 0x65 / call', 'mov esi, 0x64 / call' = CameraRight/Left/Backward (102/101/100), matching guide.md 'GetInputValue is called 4 times next to each other with the command ids 99, 100, 101, 102'

key_addresses.what: Input command registration table — proves the Windows command IDs carry over unchanged to Linux
key_addresses.evidence: bg3q.py dis 0x04146530: 'mov dword ptr [r14], 0x9d' immediately before 'lea rax, [rip - 0x26bd910] ; str CharacterMoveForward'; next block 'mov dword ptr [r14], 0x9e' before str 'CharacterMoveBackward'. BG3WASD guide.md predicted 'Should be 157, if it doesn't change. This is 0x9D'. Registration sites are 0x7e apart: 0x04146560/0x041465de/0x0414665c/0x041466da for Forward/Backward/Left/Right.

key_addresses.what: The single SDL_PollEvent call site = the game's PollInput function; the interception point bg3se and BG3WASD both use
key_addresses.evidence: sqlite3 'select count(*) from xrefs join symbols on dst=id where name=SDL_PollEvent' -> 1, site 0x02e9e7c8, rtype 4 (R_X86_64_PLT32). SDL_GetWindowGrab is called at 0x02e9f06f and 0x02e9f9e7 in the same region — BG3WASD guide.md: 'In the PollInput function, also SDL_GetWindowGrab is called twice.'

key_addresses.what: LoadInputConfig — the function that reads the keybind JSON that BG3WASD rewrites to implement movement
key_addresses.evidence: bg3q.py str inputremap -> 0x01b0efae 'inputremap_p1.json' used at 0x03b3b1f4 (also p2/p3/p4 at 0x03b3b229/0x03b3b261/0x03b3b299). guide.md: 'Search for the string inputremap_p1.json. It should only have one xref and that is inside the function I name LoadInputConfig.'

key_addresses.what: Second movement-input reader with a cmove-selected alternate command set (0x9d/0x9e/0x9f vs 0x68/0x69/0x6c)
key_addresses.evidence: bg3q.py dis 0x290a850: 'mov r15d,0x9f / mov r12d,0x9d / mov r13d,0x9e' then 'mov eax,0x6c / cmove r15d,eax', 'mov eax,0x68 / cmove r12d,eax', 'mov eax,0x69 / cmove r13d,eax', all feeding call 0x2d1d880. Suggests a mode switch (likely controller vs keyboard) selecting which command IDs are read.

key_addresses.what: Inside ecl::EocClient::HandleError — recovers the MANGLED NAME of an anonymous Larian function, and is one of bg3se's 99 required anchors (ecl__EoCClient__HandleError)
key_addresses.evidence: sqlite3 shows symbol '.L__FUNCTION__._ZN3ecl9EocClient11HandleErrorERKN2ls16TranslatedStringEbS4_N3eoc18EMessageBoxLocalIdE'; bg3q.py to <that symbol> -> '[1 references] 0x05a41fda'. There are 206 .L__FUNCTION__ and 11,375 .L__PRETTY_FUNCTION__ statics; 47 .L__FUNCTION__ are ecl/esv/eoc-scoped. This is a naming channel Norbyte does not have on Windows.

key_addresses.what: Use site of the FixedString GUID d65cf1b6-... = bg3se's ls::ModuleSettings::IsModded anchor (achievement gate)
key_addresses.evidence: bg3q.py str d65cf1b6 -> 0x01a5631f 'd65cf1b6-23a8-f0db-0a56-4b479a559748' used at 0x040905cd. Norbyte's BinaryMappings.xml uses this same GUID as the Condition for the IsModded mapping; ahungry (issue #539) could not find its xref in Ghidra — we get it by reloc for free.

key_addresses.what: Use site of 'LoadWarnings' — ahungry's stated navigation anchor for finding the modded-save warning path on Linux
key_addresses.evidence: bg3q.py str LoadWarnings -> 0x01932514 used at 0x0320c4db (single site). ahungry, bg3se issue #539: 'eventually hit a function with some wonderful string literals like LoadWarnings - on the linux binary there is only a single LoadWarnings string'. He spent ~20 hours; we resolve it in one query.

key_addresses.what: Game build string 4.1.1.7398727 — identifies our binary's exact version for cross-referencing prior art
key_addresses.evidence: bg3q.py str '^4\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' -> single hit '4.1.1.7398727', used at 6 sites. Corroborated by bg3se-macos docs/PORTING.md, which names 7398727 as a supported build ('BinkManager::LoadVideo ... stayed at 0x10390b6cc through 7209685 and moved to 0x103916380 in 7398727') — i.e. the macOS SE targets the same game version as our Linux ELF.

hook_points.where: LD_PRELOAD .so interposing SDL_PollEvent (game's only call site: 0x02e9e7c8, R_X86_64_PLT32 against libSDL2.so)
hook_points.how: Exactly bg3se's SDLManager design, ported: keep a queue of synthetic SDL_Events; on each SDL_PollEvent, drain the queue first, else call the real one via dlsym(RTLD_NEXT) and post-process. bg3se's BG3Extender/Extender/Client/SDL.cpp SDLPollEventHooked returns injected events before ever calling the wrapped function — that is a pure userspace queue, no SDL_PushEvent needed, which matters because the game does NOT import SDL_PushEvent. On Linux this needs zero code patching: the game resolves SDL_PollEvent through the PLT and our preloaded .so wins symbol lookup order.
hook_points.risk: The game may cache the function pointer (it does not appear to — single PLT-relative call site). SDL2 built with SDL_DYNAMIC_API routes internal calls through a jump table, so interposing the exported symbol catches the game's calls but not SDL-internal ones (irrelevant here). Steam's own overlay also preloads; must chain LD_PRELOAD rather than overwrite it (ahungry's bg3-linux-ae.sh does exactly this: LD_PRELOAD="...${LD_PRELOAD:+:$LD_PRELOAD}").

hook_points.where: inputremap_p1.json on disk — no code at all
hook_points.how: BG3WASD's actual movement mechanism. src/InputconfigPatcher.cpp calls UpdateData(data, "CharacterMoveForward", "CameraForward", ...) for all four axes: it copies whatever keys are bound to CameraForward/Backward/Left/Right onto CharacterMoveForward/Backward/Left/Right. The engine already routes those four commands (IDs 157-160, confirmed 0x9d at 0x04146530 in OUR binary) into the analog-movement path. This is a data change to a JSON file the game reads at 0x03b3b1f4 — it survives every patch and needs no injection whatsoever.
hook_points.risk: Alone it does nothing: the game gates that path on a controller-mode flag, which is why BG3WASD also ships WASDUnlockPatch. Also BG3WASD had to hook LoadInputConfig/AfterChangingKeybindInMenu to re-apply the patch whenever the game rewrites the file from its keybind UI.

hook_points.where: The controller-mode gate guarding the WASD movement path (Linux location NOT yet found)
hook_points.how: BG3WASD's WASDUnlockPatch NOPs a `cmp`/`jz` on a global byte the guide names IsInControllerMode, inside the predicate function called at the top of UpdateWasdMove. On Linux, start from the two movement readers I located (0x2c75cd0 and 0x0290a850) and walk callers; note 0x0290a850 already contains a cmove that switches between command-ID sets 0x9d/0x9e/0x9f and 0x68/0x69/0x6c, which is a mode branch and a strong lead. Native Camera Tweaks finds the same global by pattern '80 3D ?? ?? ?? ?? ?? 74 22' (cmp byte ptr [rip+X], imm8 / jz).
hook_points.risk: Not yet verified in our binary — this is the one load-bearing piece of the WASD design I could not confirm statically. clang's codegen may have folded the check differently than MSVC. A NOP patch also needs mprotect and is version-specific; prefer expressing it as a reloc-anchored offset rather than a byte pattern.

hook_points.where: Call-site rewriting of `call rel32` at known relocation sites, e.g. the four GetInputValue calls at 0x2c75ce4 / 0x2c75cf8 / 0x2c75d0c / 0x2c75d20
hook_points.how: This is precisely what both BG3WASD and Native Camera Tweaks do — DKUtil's `dku::Hook::write_call<5>(callSiteAddress, MyFunc)` rewrites one 5-byte call instruction, NOT the function prologue (see NCT src/Hooks.h lines 185-259: eight separate write_call<5> installs). Their whole difficulty is *finding* those call-site addresses by pattern; we already have them as literal addresses. Add the PIE load bias from dl_iterate_phdr and patch. This gives per-call-site granularity — you can hook the movement read without disturbing the 54 other GetInputValue callers.
hook_points.risk: Requires mprotect(PROT_WRITE|PROT_EXEC) on a text page and must be done before/while the game is single-threaded, or with the target thread quiesced. Redirecting a call from a hot per-frame path costs a branch mispredict at worst. Each address is build-specific (ours is 4.1.1.7398727) — but so is every approach; the difference is ours regenerates by re-running the reloc query, not by re-doing RE.

hook_points.where: Inline detour of GetInputValue itself at 0x2d1d880 using funchook / Dobby / frida-gum
hook_points.how: Single choke point for ALL input reads (58 call sites). Return a synthesised axis value for command IDs 157-160 when your WASD state says so, delegate to the original otherwise. funchook (kubo/funchook) supports Linux x86_64 and handles the trampoline/relocation of overwritten prologue instructions; frida-gum's Interceptor is the heavier but better-tested option; bg3se-macos chose Dobby for the same job on ARM64.
hook_points.risk: Prologue-splicing needs a correct instruction-length decoder and is riskier than call-site rewriting on a clang-optimised binary that may have jump targets inside the first 5 bytes. Also fires for all 58 callers including UI/menu paths, so your filter must be exact. Prefer call-site rewriting where you know the sites; reserve inline detours for functions with no enumerable call sites.

hook_points.where: Proxy or replace libSDL2.so wholesale (DT_NEEDED entry confirmed by readelf -d)
hook_points.how: The Linux analogue of what Windows Native Mod Loader does: it ships a replacement SDL2.dll (and bink2w64.dll) alongside the game. On Linux this is easier and reversible — either ship a shim libSDL2.so that dlopens the real one, or use SDL's own officially-supported SDL_DYNAMIC_API environment variable, which points SDL at a replacement library via SDL_DYNAPI_entry() filling a jump table (docs/README-dynapi.md, vendored in BG3WASD's own extern/SDL2).
hook_points.risk: SDL_DYNAMIC_API only works if the shipped libSDL2.so was built with dynapi enabled (default upstream, but I could NOT verify — we don't have the .so). Replacing the library file touches the game install, which Yet-Another-BG3-Native-Mod-Loader explicitly criticises as maintenance burden. LD_PRELOAD achieves the same interception without touching any game file.

hook_points.where: libOsiris.so exported symbols, for a scripting/event layer
hook_points.how: bg3se-macos hooks libOsiris.dylib because it 'exports clean C/C++ symbols we can hook' — 1,013 symbols including _ZN7COsiris8InitGameEv, _ZN7COsiris4LoadER12COsiSmartBuf, _DebugHook, _CreateRule, _DefineFunction, _SetInitSection. libOsiris.so is a DT_NEEDED of our binary, so the Linux equivalents are almost certainly exported and directly interposable via LD_PRELOAD with no pattern scanning at all.
hook_points.risk: Unverified — we do not have libOsiris.so, only the DT_NEEDED entry. bg3se-macos also warns that when hooking C++ member functions 'the return value must be captured and returned from the hook. Failing to do so causes the game to fail silently.' Osiris is the story/quest layer, not the movement layer, so this is orthogonal to WASD.

hook_points.where: Vulkan implicit layer for any in-game overlay (ImGui-style debug UI)
hook_points.how: bg3se renders its console with ImGui via ImGui_ImplSDL2_InitForVulkan. On Linux, an implicit Vulkan layer (a JSON manifest in ~/.local/share/vulkan/implicit_layer.d) is the officially-sanctioned interception mechanism — this is how MangoHud and vkBasalt work, no patching involved.
hook_points.risk: Our binary imports zero vk* symbols (sqlite: 'select count(*) from symbols where name like vk%' -> 0), so Vulkan is reached indirectly, most likely via SDL_Vulkan_GetVkGetInstanceProcAddr or dlopen of libvulkan. A layer still intercepts correctly regardless, but you cannot hook a vk* PLT entry that does not exist. Input capture from an overlay must coordinate with whatever SDL_PollEvent filtering you install.

hook_points.where: Per-version address table generated from the reloc/symbol DB, instead of a pattern database
hook_points.how: Copy bg3se-macos's tools/port_offsets.py + offset_manifest.json model: record each needed address by SYMBOL plus its resolution method, and regenerate the table per build. Their PORTING.md states plainly: 'The macOS BG3 binary ships with its symbol table... So almost every address the extender needs can be found by name with nm, no Ghidra required. (Norbyte's Windows extender needs heavy pattern-scanning because the Windows binary is stripped.)' Our situation is the same but stronger, because --emit-relocs gives exact xrefs for the anonymous functions too.
hook_points.risk: Their doc names the real failure modes and they apply to us verbatim: 'ABI CHANGED — the symbol resolved, but its signature no longer matches the C wrapper that calls it... Address validity is not ABI validity'; 'AMBIGUOUS — the symbol matched more than one address'; and struct field offsets still require one-time Ghidra work and can silently break when Larian restructures a class.

negative_results: There is NO Linux-native Script Extender and no maintainer intent to build one. bg3se issue #530 'SE & SteamDeck Native 9-23 Update' (opened 2025-09-23) is still open with no maintainer commitment; the substantive comments are from users, not Norbyte. Norbyte's own reply lives in issue #539 (2025-11-13): 'The Linux version is built with a different compiler (either GCC or LLVM) so the generated assembly will probably be very different... it is likely that the old patterns will not match code in the Linux binary.' The macOS PR #477 was closed unmerged.

bg3se's entire function-discovery layer does NOT carry over. BinaryMappings.xml is 69 <Mapping> blocks / 101 <Target> entries resolving 99 distinct symbols, all as MSVC x86-64 byte patterns with a single Version="4.47.63.76" — e.g. '4c 8b 74 24 68 // mov r14, [rsp+48h+arg_18]' for ls__GlobalAllocator. Windows-calling-convention register allocation (rcx/rdx/r8/r9) is baked into every pattern; our binary is SysV (rdi/rsi/rdx/rcx). Zero of it is reusable. What IS reusable is the *target list* — those 99 symbol names are a validated inventory of what an extender actually needs to reach.

Byte-pattern scanning is empirically unreliable even on Linux. I searched our .text (vaddr 0x218be00, size 0x565c316) for all four historical pattern generations from ahungry/bg3-linux-ae: 'MODDED 20260327' (27 1b 04 0f 94 c0), 'MODDED 20260216' (76 1b 04 ...), 'MODDED 20251120' (62 1a 04 ...), and the original (0c 1b 04 ...) — 0 hits each. Likewise MODDED2 (all three variants a3/a5/a6 00 84 c0 0f 84 c3 00 00 00) and MODDED3 (4d/4e 01 84 c0 74 0b) — 0 hits each. The author had to re-derive these three times in four months. Our binary is 4.1.1.7398727.

BG3 WASD movement is NOT implemented by synthesised mouse clicks, and not by any move API. Ch4nKyy/BG3WASD src/InputconfigPatcher.cpp rebinds the four CharacterMove* commands to the CameraForward/Backward/Left/Right keys in inputremap_pN.json, and doc/guide.md states the whole design in three lines: 'Assign the CharacterMoveForward etc commands, which are usually for analog controller movement, to some keyboard keys in the input config / The game usually ignores this input when the controller UI is inactive, but WASDUnlockPatch overrides this check / Everything else is just QoL and bonus features.' AutoHotkey appears only as an OPTIONAL extra for caps-lock mode toggle and shift+W autorun — not as the movement mechanism.

The game does not import SDL_PushEvent or SDL_SetRelativeMouseMode. Of 71 SDL_* symbols in the binary, a targeted query for ('SDL_PollEvent','SDL_PushEvent','SDL_PeepEvents','SDL_SetRelativeMouseMode','SDL_WarpMouseInWindow','SDL_GetWindowGrab','SDL_GameControllerGetAxis','SDL_GetKeyboardState') returned only SDL_PollEvent, SDL_WarpMouseInWindow and SDL_GetWindowGrab. This kills any design that assumes you can shove events into the game's queue by calling the game's own SDL_PushEvent — and it is exactly why bg3se's SDLManager::InjectEvent maintains its own vector drained inside the SDL_PollEvent hook rather than calling SDL_PushEvent. (A preloaded .so can of course still link SDL_PushEvent itself, as BG3WASD's InputFaker does.)

No vk* symbols at all (sqlite count = 0), so Vulkan is not reachable through the PLT; it must be loaded indirectly. Any overlay plan must go through a Vulkan implicit layer or through SDL, not through interposing vkQueuePresentKHR on the main binary.

There is essentially no native-Linux BG3 native-code modding community. A GitHub search for BG3+Linux repos returns mod *managers* (mac-bg3mm, BG3ModManager-LinuxLauncher, OneHornModManager, bg3-linux-mod-manager) and exactly one native code mod: ahungry/bg3-linux-ae. Nexus mod 23896 'Linux Native Camera Tweaks' exists and is described as native Linux, but nexusmods.com returns HTTP 403 to automated fetch and I could not locate source or confirm its injection technique — treat its existence as confirmed and its method as unknown. Larian's own position (larian.com FAQ, and the Steam depot being Deck-flagged) is that the native build is Steam Deck only and unsupported elsewhere; the community guidance is 'native is faster IF you only use .pak mods and no Script Extender'.

The Windows DLL-proxy injection concept has no direct analogue worth copying. bg3se's BG3Updater/DWriteWrapper.cpp LoadLibrary's the real system DWrite.dll and forwards DWriteCreateFactory; dllmain.cpp runs StartUpdaterThread() on DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH; Updater.cpp then fetches a manifest and picks a build via FindResourceVersionWithOverrides(resourceName, gameVersion, config). None of the proxy machinery is needed on Linux — LD_PRELOAD with an __attribute__((constructor)) does the same job in three lines (see bg3_linux_ae.cpp init_patch). The *versioned-manifest* idea is worth keeping; the DLL-proxy plumbing is not.

Norbyte's symbol-recovery trick is unavailable to us but also unnecessary. He told issue #539: 'A lot of the functions were mapped through the Toolkit binaries; the toolkit is not a single .exe but is split into many DLL-s and exports a lot of the internal game functions using names; it also has assertions enabled (which is why we know the function is called esv::SavegameManager::ThrowError).' SymbolTableGenerator/SymbolTableGenerator.cpp confirms this — it is a DIA/msdia140.dll PDB reader. We have no Toolkit and no PDB; we have .rela.text plus 206 .L__FUNCTION__ and 11,375 .L__PRETTY_FUNCTION__ statics, 47 of which are ecl/esv/eoc-scoped mangled names, which recover Larian function identities directly (verified: ecl::EocClient::HandleError -> 0x05a41fda).
open_questions: Where is the controller-mode gate in the Linux binary? This is the single load-bearing unknown for a WASD port. BG3WASD NOPs a cmp/jz on a global byte inside the predicate at the top of UpdateWasdMove; Native Camera Tweaks locates the same global with pattern '80 3D ?? ?? ?? ?? ?? 74 22'. Concrete next step: walk callers of the two movement readers I found (0x2c75cd0, 0x0290a850) and examine the cmove at 0x0290a876-0x0290a892 that switches command IDs between 0x9d/0x9e/0x9f and 0x68/0x69/0x6c — that branch looks like the mode selector.

Is the inputremap JSON path alone sufficient on the native Linux build? If Larian's Linux build reads a different config location (the native save path is ~/.local/share/Larian Studios/Baldur's Gate 3/ per Larian's FAQ, not the Proton prefix), the pure-data half of the WASD technique may need a different file path. Cannot verify without the game data.

Was the shipped libSDL2.so built with SDL_DYNAMIC_API enabled? That decides whether the officially-supported, zero-patching SDL_DYNAMIC_API=/path/to/mylibSDL2.so override is available as an alternative to LD_PRELOAD. Needs the actual .so from a game install.

Does libOsiris.so export the same clean C++ symbols on Linux that bg3se-macos found in libOsiris.dylib (1,013 symbols incl. COsiris::InitGame, COsiris::Load, _DefineFunction)? If yes, an Osiris event/scripting layer is nearly free via LD_PRELOAD interposition. Needs the .so.

What technique does Nexus mod 23896 'Linux Native Camera Tweaks' actually use — LD_PRELOAD, a patched ELF, or something else? It is the only other known native-Linux BG3 code mod besides bg3-linux-ae and would be direct competition/collaboration. nexusmods.com blocks automated fetch (HTTP 403); this needs a manual browser visit or contacting the author.

How stable are our reloc-derived addresses across Larian hotfixes? bg3se-macos's port_offsets.py assumes a mostly-uniform segment shift with named exceptions ('component_data_shift validated' vs 'REJECTED... migrate TypeIds independently by exact symbol'). We should test our address table against a second BG3 Linux build to learn whether the same uniform-shift heuristic holds for the ELF, before committing to it.

Norbyte's 99 mapped symbols are a validated 'what an extender needs' inventory. How many of them can we resolve in our binary today via strings/relocs/.L__FUNCTION__ statics? Worth running as a systematic sweep — it would quantify the gap between us and feature-parity with the Windows SE, the same way bg3se-macos publishes a per-API parity matrix.

Should we upstream anything? bg3se issue #539 has an active audience (four separate users asking for native Linux support through 2026-04), and tdimino/bg3se-macos has solved the non-Windows SE problem once already with a documented, reusable porting methodology. Reusing their offset-manifest tooling — or coordinating so a Linux backend lands in the same project — may be far cheaper than a from-scratch framework.

summary: The client camera is ECS-driven: every camera entity carries ls::CameraComponent (0xb0 bytes; byte 0 = owning-behavior mode enum, observed 8=game, 11=scene, 12=spectator; byte 0x14 = active flag), ecl::EocCameraBehavior (0x40 bytes; int16 player index at +0x38), ls::TransformComponent (0x28: quat@+0x00, pos@+0x10, scale@+0x1c), plus one behavior component — ecl::GameCameraBehavior (0x258 bytes) for the gameplay camera. The per-entity game-camera update is the anonymous function at 0x2c7d3a0 (dispatched from the CameraSystem update at 0x221aac0 when mode==8); it stores yaw NOT as an angle but as two normalized XZ direction vectors in GameCameraBehavior (+0x70 current, +0x7c target), with a rotation-remaining accumulator in degrees at +0xac, a follow-desired direction at +0xd0, a manual-control cooldown at +0x13c, and pending "move camera here" vec3+flag channels at +0x238/+0x244 and +0x248/+0x254 that the engine itself uses to recenter the camera (committed after screen-fade completion). Follow-the-character already exists: the update resolves ecl::camera::TargetComponent entities, fetches their eoc::character::CharacterComponent/ls::TransformComponent and the splitscreen MergedFocus singleton, and steers the target direction toward them with a powf speed curve whose parameters come from mouse-vs-controller config blocks at gSettings(+0x7c4/+0x958, override +0xc80/+0xdac) under the global pointer at 0x7d9d198. All camera inputs are named, numbered input events registered at 0x4144400 (CameraCenter=0x61 … CameraRotateMouseLeft/Right=0x6d/0x6e, full FreeCamera suite 0x6f–0x86 including mouse pitch, ToggleTacticalCamera=0xd9), so mouse-look yaw exists natively for the game camera but pitch mouse-look exists only in the FreeCamera/PhotoMode path. For WASD, "forward" can be read directly from GameCameraBehavior+0x70 (XZ direction) or from the camera entity's TransformComponent quaternion.

key_addresses.what: GameCameraBehavior per-entity update function (~0x2c7d3a0-0x2c85565, anonymous). Signature: f(system_this, ecs_ctx, time*, row_ctx*); dt is time[2]. Contains all yaw/follow/zoom logic.
key_addresses.evidence: Called from the CameraSystem update at 0x221d5xx with a struct of component-row pointers; references ecl::camera::TargetComponent TypeId at 0x2c7d67e, CharacterComponent at 0x2c7da50, LevelComponent/TransformComponent at 0x2c7dc26/0x2c7dc34; sinf/cosf/atan2f/powf cluster 0x2c7ef70-0x2c80832; Ghidra decompilation of carved region recovered field usage.

summary: The controller path is real and fully mapped: BG3-Linux consumes gamepads 100% event-driven through a SINGLE SDL_PollEvent site (0x2e9e7c7) — it never polls axis state (no SDL_GameControllerGetAxis/Update imports exist), so a virtual pad is trivially injectable either via uinput (the DEVICEADDED handler at 0x2e9eade hotplug-opens any pad) or by LD_PRELOAD-interposing ~15 PLT-imported SDL functions. However, input events are tagged deviceType=3+controllerIndex and feed a single input-mode arbiter (0x500c4f0) whose only two outcomes are ActivateControllerMode (0x500bec0) and EnsureKBM (0x500c270) — byte-scan proved these are the ONLY runtime switchers — and mode change triggers a WHOLESALE Noesis UI reload: 0x5f16fc0 calls GUI::LoadApplicationResources with 'Theme/DefaultTheme_c.xaml' vs 'Theme/DefaultTheme.xaml' (plus StateMachine_c.xaml etc.), so naive virtual-pad + real mouse = constant heavyweight UI thrash between pad and KBM themes. The escape hatch: all four switch paths are guarded by two config bytes ([cfg@[base+0x7D5C040]]+0x221/+0x222 — if bit0 set, switching is suppressed), which an in-process shim can poke to pin the KBM UI. Verdict: pure uinput is a dead end for shipping; LD_PRELOAD fake-pad + mode-freeze poke is a strong prototype stepping stone, with one decisive unknown remaining (whether gameplay consumes stick→CharacterMoveForward actions while UI mode stays KBM — a 30-minute runtime test). Cheapest possible win also discovered: CharacterMoveForward/Backward/Left/Right are ordinary registered input actions (id 0x9d.., marked '- internal', excluded from rebind UI but in the same raw-input space as keyboard keys), and bindings live in data (PlayerProfiles/Eoc/keyboard_1.json), so WASD may be achievable with zero code if the binding parser accepts keyboard bindings for internal actions.

claim: LD_PRELOAD .so interposing SDL_PollEvent (single game call site 0x02e9e7c8, R_X86_64_PLT32) is a viable zero-patch hook point for a WASD mod, using a bg3se-style userspace synthetic-event queue; the game does not cache the function pointer and does not import SDL_PushEvent.
reasoning: Core claim CONFIRMED at the ELF level, with independent re-derivation. (1) SDL_PollEvent is an UND FUNC in .dynsym; readelf -rW over the ENTIRE binary shows exactly two relocations against it: the R_X86_64_JUMP_SLOT at GOT 0x7b61840 (normal PLT machinery) and one R_X86_64_PLT32 code site at 0x2e9e7c8 — no R_X86_64_GOTPCREL/GLOB_DAT anywhere, so the game never takes the function's address into a data pointer; the 'may cache' risk is definitively absent. (2) Disassembly at the site: 0x2e9e7c2 'lea rdi,[rsp+0x68]'; 0x2e9e7c7 'call SDL_PollEvent'; 'test eax,eax; je' — a while(SDL_PollEvent(&ev)) pump with a switch on event type (cmp 0x603 / range 0x650-0x655 = SDL_CONTROLLERAXISMOTION family), i.e. this one loop consumes both keyboard and controller events. (3) SDL_PushEvent is absent from .dynsym; so are SDL_PumpEvents, SDL_PeepEvents, SDL_WaitEvent(Timeout), SDL_AddEventWatch, SDL_SetEventFilter, SDL_GetKeyboardState, SDL_GetModState, SDL_GameControllerGetAxis/GetButton (71 SDL imports total). All key/controller input is therefore event-driven through this single pump — injected synthetic events reach the same consumer as real ones. (Only mouse position is polled, via imported SDL_GetGlobalMouseState — irrelevant to WASD.) (4) Interposition mechanics hold: libSDL2.so is DT_NEEDED with RUNPATH $ORIGIN; .gnu.version_r has version needs only for glibc libs (SDL symbols unversioned); LD_PRELOAD objects precede DT_NEEDED/RUNPATH libs in lookup order. The game imports dlopen/dlsym but the string literals 'SDL_PollEvent' and 'libSDL2' occur ZERO times in the binary, ruling out any runtime dlsym path to SDL — the PLT call is the game's only route. (5) Supporting addresses all verified: GetInputValue at 0x2d1d880 (my own e8-rel32 scan of .text reproduces exactly 58 call sites, including 0x2c75ce4/cf8/d0c/d20 and 0x2c82c05/c1d/c35); 0x2c75cd0 reads commands 0xa0/0x9f/0x9d/0x9e and merges via insertps at 0x2c75d2a; 0x2c82bf0 region reads 0x66/0x65/0x64 (plus 0x63 at 0x2c82c4d — the 4th camera command, matching guide.md's '4 times'); registration at 0x4146530: 'mov dword ptr [r14],0x9d' at 0x414654a then lea → str 'CharacterMoveForward' (reloc site 0x4146560); 0x290a850 region has the cmove-selected 0x9d/0x9e/0x9f vs 0x68/0x69/0x6c alternates; inputremap_p1..p4.json used at 0x3b3b1f4/0x3b3b229/0x3b3b261/0x3b3b299; 'LoadWarnings' single site 0x320c4db; GUID d65cf1b6-... at 0x40905cd; build string '4.1.1.7398727' at 0x199b5bb with 6 use sites; .L__FUNCTION__._ZN3ecl9EocClient11HandleError... exists (0x1a33642) with single ref at 0x5a41fda; counts 206 .L__FUNCTION__ / 11375 .L__PRETTY_FUNCTION__ / 47 ecl-esv-eoc-scoped all match. ERRORS FOUND (supporting context only, do not affect the hook): (a) The claim that SDL_GetWindowGrab is called at 0x02e9f06f AND 0x02e9f9e7 is FALSE — the entire binary contains exactly one SDL_GetWindowGrab call site (0x2e9f06f); the reloc at 0x2e9f9e7 is R_X86_64_PLT32 against SDL_WarpMouseInWindow (call instruction 0x2e9f9e6). The Windows 'called twice in PollInput' landmark does NOT carry over to Linux. (b) The rationale 'no SDL_PushEvent needed, which matters because the game does NOT import SDL_PushEvent' is overstated: the game's import set does not constrain the preloaded .so, which could itself resolve SDL_PushEvent from libSDL2.so via dlsym/RTLD_NEXT; the userspace queue is still the better design but the justification is not load-bearing. (c) 0x2c82bf0 and 0x290a850 are mid-function labels, not function entries (0x2c82bf0 begins with a bare jne; 0x290a850 disassembles misaligned until 0x290a859) — the claimed instruction content is present, but anyone hooking these as 'function' addresses would break; the proposal hooks SDL_PollEvent, so this is not fatal. External-repo assertions (bg3se SDL.cpp behavior, ahungry's LD_PRELOAD chaining line, Norbyte issue quotes, bg3se-macos PORTING.md) are not verifiable from the binary and were not counted for or against.
correction: Core claim stands. Corrections to supporting details: SDL_GetWindowGrab has exactly ONE call site in the Linux binary (0x2e9f06f); the site at 0x2e9f9e7 calls SDL_WarpMouseInWindow, not SDL_GetWindowGrab — the Windows 'GetWindowGrab called twice' landmark does not survive into this build. Also, 0x2c82bf0 and 0x290a850 are basic-block addresses inside larger functions, not function entry points, and the absence of SDL_PushEvent from the game's imports would not actually prevent a preloaded .so from using SDL_PushEvent itself (it can resolve it from libSDL2.so directly); the userspace queue is preferable but not forced.

summary: BG3's direct-drive movement path exists and is fully client-side: a per-player controller object literally named "MoveController" (name string at 0x1b29d3c, vtable ~0x79f4580, virtual update at 0x2c72d80) polls four analog input actions (0x9d CharacterMoveForward, 0x9e Backward, 0x9f Left, 0xa0 Right) via the input manager, builds a signed 2D vector, applies deadzone/clamp, rotates it into world space by a camera quaternion, and writes it into eoc::controller::LocomotionComponent (132 bytes: magnitude@+0x00, normalized world dir@+0x04, raw world vector@+0x10, derived near-target point = charPos+dir@+0x5c, speed@+0x80). So there IS a desired-direction vector field — direct drive is NOT expressed as a pathfinding destination; only the derived near-target point plus a heading angle (eoc::steering::SyncComponent, a single float) are streamed to the server via eocnet::CharacterSteeringMessage (msg id 0x24). Click-to-move is a separate controller ("MoveToController") and separate server task machinery (MoveTask/OsirisSteerTask strings). ecl::MovementSystem, ecl::PathingSystem (whose update body 0x241da30 is the actual per-frame position integrator over {MovementComponent, PathingComponent, SteeringComponent, Transform, optional LocomotionComponent}), ecl::controller::{Flood,Physics}System consume the LocomotionComponent. The smallest state change that makes the controlled character walk this frame is 9 bytes: the debug/forced-input override inside the input-fetch function 0x2c75c60 — write a vec2 at [ [0x7d9d198] ]+0x1394 and set the byte at +0x139c, and the character walks in that (camera-relative) direction through the entire legitimate pipeline.

dimension: hooking — the Linux hooking substrate for a BG3 native-ELF extender
summary: The binary is about as friendly a target as a 214 MB PIE gets: zero Intel CET (0 endbr64 in all 90.1 MB of .text, no .note.gnu.property), classic lazy PLT with a writable .got.plt outside GNU_RELRO, no BIND_NOW, and no anti-tamper whatsoever — every ptrace/prctl call site in the file belongs to crashpad, and the one TracerPid check in main() exists to *disable* the crash reporter under a debugger. Load bias is trivial because the first PT_LOAD has p_vaddr 0, so live = base + static_addr; I verified dl_iterate_phdr, getauxval(AT_PHDR) and /proc/self/maps all return the identical bias. .symtab/.strtab/.rela.text all sit past the end of every PT_LOAD (highest mapped file offset 0x7b5ff08; .symtab starts at 0xc7ec8a8), so dlsym can never see Larian internals — but preading 13.9 MB of symtab+strtab from /proc/self/exe and resolving arbitrary needles takes 27 ms, which is free. The executable exports only 4 dynamic symbols, so LD_PRELOAD cannot interpose any game function (I proved empirically that an exe-defined symbol beats a preload, which kills pthread_create interposition specifically); inline hooking with a 5-byte rel32 into a near "island" is required, and I built and ran a working end-to-end preload that resolves an unexported .symtab symbol, allocates a trampoline within ±2 GB, and diverts the function. The biggest non-obvious findings: our handler in the .so lands ~26 TB away from the game's .text so a bare rel32 always overflows and a 14-byte absolute jump island is mandatory; the game fork()s at main+0x32f and runs as a *child* under a waitpid supervisor unless --no-crash-reporter is passed or a debugger is attached; and libOsiris.so is a DT_NEEDED with RUNPATH $ORIGIN, so a drop-in shim library (proven working) gives us load-without-LD_PRELOAD plus free interposition of all 32 COsiris PLT imports.

hook_points.where: Load-bias resolution, at .so constructor time
hook_points.how: Use dl_iterate_phdr and take the first callback whose dlpi_name[0]=='\0' → dlpi_addr is the bias. Because the first PT_LOAD has p_vaddr 0, live = bias + static_addr with no further arithmetic. Fall back to getauxval(AT_PHDR) minus PT_PHDR's p_vaddr, or the first /proc/self/maps line whose path matches readlink(/proc/self/exe).
hook_points.risk: Essentially none. Do NOT use dladdr(&main) — main is a .symtab-only local and dladdr resolves via .dynsym. Do not assume /proc/self/maps line ordering if the loader ever splits the image; match by resolved path.

hook_points.where: Unexported Larian/third-party symbol resolution, in the .so constructor
hook_points.how: open("/proc/self/exe"), pread the section headers, find SHT_SYMTAB and its sh_link strtab, pread both (3.49 MB + 10.37 MB), single pass matching against a hash set of needles. Measured on this exact 213.8 MB file: pread 9.7 ms + one scan 16.9 ms = 27 ms total, and it is flat whether you resolve 500 or 3000 names. Building a full name→value hash of all 152,400 named symbols instead costs 42 ms and 8 MB. Either is free relative to game load time.
hook_points.risk: This only reaches the 45k third-party/libc++/mimalloc symbols and a handful of globals — ~90% of .text is anonymous Larian code with no name at all. Also: if Larian ever ships a stripped build this path evaporates, so detect SHT_SYMTAB absence and degrade gracefully. Reading /proc/self/exe on Steam Deck cold-cache adds disk I/O for 13.9 MB.

hook_points.where: Anonymous Larian functions (the interesting 90%)
hook_points.how: Ship a build-id-keyed offset table generated OFFLINE from bg3.db. Key it on the 20-byte .note.gnu.build-id at vaddr 0x31c (mapped, cheap to read). Generate targets by the reloc-graph method proven above: anchor on a distinctive .L.str, follow xrefs, and for anonymous callees query `xrefs where dst = <.text SECTION sym> and addend = target - 4 - 0x218be00`.

hook_points.risk: Measured on this binary: a 12-byte masked pattern over 90.1 MB costs 110 ms naive / 40 ms memmem-accelerated, and the SDL_PollEvent-loop pattern I tried was NOT unique — 24 hits. Fifty patterns scanned independently would be 2-5 s of startup. Every pattern must be uniqueness-verified offline against this binary before shipping. Treat as last resort, not the primary mechanism.

hook_points.where: Inline hooking of any game function — the core mechanism
hook_points.how: 5-byte `E9 rel32` at the function entry, jumping to a 14-byte absolute-jump ISLAND (`FF 25 00 00 00 00` + `.quad handler`) allocated within ±2 GB of .text; the island then jumps to your handler in the .so. Trampoline = stolen bytes + `E9 rel32` back to entry+N, also placed in the near arena. Because .text spans only 90.1 MB, a single 2 MB arena mmap'd anywhere near the image serves every one of the 43,315 functions.
hook_points.risk: THE island is mandatory, not optional — I measured the actual distance from the game .text to a handler inside an LD_PRELOAD .so at +28,449,870,957,659 bytes (~26 TB); a bare rel32 silently truncates and segfaults (I reproduced exactly that crash before adding the island). Sample of 4000 functions: 15.1% have a RIP-relative operand and 12.8% have a rel branch/call inside the first ≥5 bytes, so the trampoline builder MUST relocate disp32 and rel32 — a naive length-decoder is not enough. Only 41 of 43,315 named functions are unpatchable (size + trailing int3 padding < 5). mprotect cost is negligible: 11.3 µs per page RWX→write→restore, or 1.5 ms to flip the whole 90 MB.

hook_points.where: Choice of hooking library
hook_points.how: funchook (kubo/funchook) or Dobby. Both allocate trampolines within ±2 GB automatically, do the mprotect dance, and relocate RIP-relative and rel-branch prologue instructions. If hand-rolling, pair a real decoder (Zydis) with explicit disp32/rel32 fixup and reserve the near arena at constructor time before the heap grows.
hook_points.risk: subhook is the wrong choice here: its length decoding is minimal and would mangle the 15.1% of prologues with RIP-relative operands. I could not install or test funchook/Dobby in this environment, so their behaviour on THIS binary's prologues is unverified — validate against a corpus of real BG3 entry points before trusting it. Also check each library's license against your distribution plans.

hook_points.where: Intel CET / endbr64
hook_points.how: Nothing to do. Patch the first byte of the function directly; there is no endbr64 landing pad to preserve and no IBT to trip.
hook_points.risk: None for the game binary. But note that libc/libSDL2 from a modern host or the Steam runtime ARE built with -fcf-protection, so if you ever inline-hook into a *system* library your island's indirect jump must land on an endbr64. Keep game hooks and libc hooks on separate code paths.

hook_points.where: Imported functions (808 PLT slots): SDL_*, the 32 COsiris entry points, Steam, libc
hook_points.how: Plain LD_PRELOAD interposition. Define the symbol in your .so, recover the real one with dlsym(RTLD_NEXT, …). No inline hooking, no mprotect, no address table, survives every patch. SDL_PollEvent is the single best tick: one call site (0x2e9e7c7), a `while(SDL_PollEvent(&ev))` drain loop, so the call that returns 0 is a clean end-of-frame-input hook.
hook_points.risk: Does NOT work for pthread_create — the executable defines and exports it at 0x3357fc0 and the exe always wins the global symbol search; I verified this empirically with a repro where an exe-defined symbol beat the preload. If you want that one, inline-hook it. Also: any function the game resolves itself via dlsym(RTLD_NEXT) bypasses your definition by design.

hook_points.where: GOT interposition of PLT imports without LD_PRELOAD
hook_points.how: Walk the mapped _DYNAMIC for DT_JMPREL/DT_PLTRELSZ/DT_SYMTAB/DT_STRTAB (all four are inside LOAD[0], file offsets 0x74ac88 / 0x340 / 0x5944 — no disk I/O needed), find the JUMP_SLOT whose symbol name you want, and overwrite the 8-byte .got.plt entry.
hook_points.risk: Free of mprotect because .got.plt (0x7b615b0–0x7b62f08) is outside GNU_RELRO (which ends at 0x7af8000) — verified by containment arithmetic. But there is no DT_BIND_NOW, so binding is LAZY: before the first call, the GOT slot holds the push/jmp-back-to-PLT0 address, not the resolved function. Never save the pre-hook GOT value as your "original" — get the real target with dlsym instead. Also, this only redirects calls that go through THIS module's GOT; calls originating inside libSDL2 itself are unaffected.

hook_points.where: Getting loaded at all — option A: Steam launch options
hook_points.how: `LD_PRELOAD=/full/path/to/libbg3x.so %command%` in the game's Steam launch options. %command% expands to the whole launcher command line, so the variable is set on the outermost process and inherited down.
hook_points.risk: Under the Steam Linux Runtime (pressure-vessel) the game runs in a container where host paths are remapped; a path inside the game's own install directory is bind-mounted and survives, a path under host /usr or /home may not. Our .so must also be ABI-compatible with the container's glibc, not the host's. I could not test any of this here — Steam-container behaviour is documentation/experience, not something I verified in this binary.

hook_points.where: Getting loaded at all — option B: DT_NEEDED shim (recommended)
hook_points.how: Rename the shipped libOsiris.so to libOsiris_real.so, and drop in our own libOsiris.so built with `-Wl,-soname,libOsiris.so -Wl,--no-as-needed -lOsiris_real -Wl,-rpath,$ORIGIN`. I BUILT AND RAN this: the shim's constructor fires, and every symbol the game imports still resolves transparently through the real library pulled in as the shim's own dependency. Adding a definition of an Osiris symbol to the shim makes the shim win the search order, with dlsym(RTLD_NEXT) reaching the real one — also verified running. This is the ELF equivalent of the Windows DLL-proxy trick and needs no LD_PRELOAD, no launch options, and works identically inside a Steam container.
hook_points.risk: The game's DT_RUNPATH is `$ORIGIN`, so the shim must live in the game directory and carry its own `$ORIGIN` runpath (mine did). You must not accidentally strip or reorder the DT_NEEDED. Breaks if Larian ever adds an integrity check on the game directory (none exists today). Renaming a shipped file means Steam's "verify integrity" will restore libOsiris.so and clobber the shim — the installer must handle that.

hook_points.where: When to run: constructor ordering
hook_points.how: Both an LD_PRELOAD .so and the DT_NEEDED shim run their constructors BEFORE the executable's init_array. I verified the ordering empirically (`[preload] constructor` → `[exe] init_array entry 1` → `[exe] init_array LAST` → `[exe] main()`) on glibc 2.39. That is the ideal moment to install hooks: single-threaded, nothing initialised yet, no locks held.
hook_points.risk: The binary has 24,135 init_array entries (INIT_ARRAYSZ 193080 / 8), so at constructor time essentially nothing is set up — ECS type indices at 0x7b6fed0+ are all still zero. Anything needing live game state must be deferred to a hooked runtime function. Bigger trap: main() fork()s at 0x5a0a5ff, so your constructor state is inherited by BOTH the supervisor and the game child. Do not spawn threads, take locks, or open sockets in the constructor — a mutex held by a thread that does not survive fork deadlocks the child. Defer heavy init to the first SDL_PollEvent tick.

hook_points.where: Debugging: neutralising crashpad
hook_points.how: Three verified levers, in order of preference. (1) Pass `--no-crash-reporter` on the command line — CFG-verified to skip both fork() and the crashpad StartHandler block. (2) Attach a debugger: main calls IsDebuggerPresent at 0x5a0a462 and takes the same skip path, so gdb/lldb automatically disables the reporter. (3) Rename or remove `<gamedir>/handler` — StartHandler then fails with 'failed to start crashpad client' and no signal handlers are installed. As a runtime fallback, re-sigaction SIGSEGV/SIGBUS/SIGILL/SIGFPE/SIGABRT/SIGTRAP to SIG_DFL after startup, since the only install site is 0x515842b.
hook_points.risk: With the crash reporter active the game runs as a fork() child, so plain `gdb ./bg3` lands on the waitpid supervisor — you need `set follow-fork-mode child`, or just use --no-crash-reporter to get a single process. Note that (2) means a debugger changes the process topology, so a bug that only reproduces under the forked configuration will vanish under gdb.

hook_points.where: ABI matching for our .so
hook_points.how: The game statically links libc++ 18.1 (1,124 _ZNSt3__2 symbols; the 16 non-__2 std:: names carry the libc++ `B8ne180100` ABI tag) and does NOT link libstdc++ at all — no GLIBCXX/CXXABI version needs. Combined with only 4 exported dynamic symbols, there is ZERO C++ symbol collision risk: our .so may freely link libstdc++ or its own libc++. Max glibc requirement is GLIBC_2.28, so build against the oldest glibc you intend to support.
hook_points.risk: There is no shared C++ runtime, so exceptions, RTTI, std::string/std::vector layouts and typeinfo must NEVER cross the boundary. More concretely: the game's `operator new` at 0x2454490 is mimalloc-backed via TLS `_mi_heap_default`; any memory you hand to the game must come from ITS operator new (resolve 0x2454490/0x2397530 from .symtab) and any pointer it hands you must go back to its operator delete. Mixing heaps will corrupt mimalloc's page metadata. Also, do not link your own copy of mimalloc.

negative_results: NO Intel CET / IBT. I scanned all 0x565c316 bytes of .text for f3 0f 1e fa: exactly 0 occurrences (and 0 endbr32). readelf -n shows only NT_GNU_ABI_TAG and NT_GNU_BUILD_ID — there is no .note.gnu.property, so no GNU_PROPERTY_X86_FEATURE_1_IBT/SHSTK. The .plt is the classic non-IBT form (`ff 35 <got+8> / ff 25 <got+16>` then `ff 25 / 68 idx / e9`). Naive entry-point patching is safe and no endbr64 landing pad is needed.

NO anti-tamper, NO anti-debug, NO self-integrity checking. Every one of the 9 ptrace call sites belongs to crashpad (Ptracer::GetThreadInfo/ReadUpTo/ReadLastBytes, PtraceAttach, PtraceDetach) and all 6 prctl call sites belong to crashpad (ScopedPrSetDumpable, InitializeSignalStackForThread, WaitForCrashDumpComplete). mprotect is called from exactly 2 sites, one of them crashpad's signal-stack setup. A string search for tamper/integrity/self-check/anti-cheat/debugger-detected returned nothing. The only /proc/self/status + TracerPid read (0x3812840) is used to DISABLE the crash reporter under a debugger — the opposite of anti-debug.

LD_PRELOAD cannot interpose ANY Larian game function. .dynsym has 823 entries of which 819 are UND; the only defined entries are pthread_create, _edata, __bss_start and _end. There is no game function to interpose. Worse, I proved with a 3-file repro (exe + liba.so + preload.so) that a symbol defined by the EXECUTABLE beats LD_PRELOAD entirely — the exe copy ran both with and without the preload — so pthread_create at 0x3357fc0 specifically is off-limits to preloading.

The reloc-derived cross-reference graph is NOT available at runtime. .rela.text (71 MB, file offset 0x7b5ff08) has sh_addr 0 and lies past the highest mapped file offset (0x7b5ff08 is exactly the end of the last PT_LOAD). Same for .symtab (0xc7ec8a8) and .strtab (0xcb69b13). Anything that depends on the xref graph must be precomputed offline.

No full RELRO and no BIND_NOW. DT_FLAGS_1 is `PIE` only; there is no DT_BIND_NOW and no DF_BIND_NOW. GNU_RELRO ends at 0x7af8000 while .got.plt starts at 0x7b615b0, so the PLT GOT stays writable for the process lifetime.

The int3-padding hot-patch trick is not general here. Measuring int3 runs immediately before all 43,315 sized FUNC entries: only 13.6% have ≥14 bytes of preceding padding, and the distribution is nearly uniform from 0 to 15 bytes (5.5% have none at all). Function starts are 16-byte aligned in 42,963 of 43,315 cases, so the padding is whatever the previous function's tail left over.

No native plugin or mod-loading mechanism exists. The only dlopen call sites are Wwise plugin DLLs, libasound.so.2, libpulse.so.0, libcuda.so (PhysX GPU) and libvulkan.so/.1 — all third-party. There is no Larian-authored extension load path, so LD_PRELOAD or the DT_NEEDED shim are the only entries.

No libstdc++ anywhere. DT_NEEDED lists libSDL2, libsteam_api, libBink2x64, libOsiris, libdl, libnvsdk_ngx, libm, libpthread, libssl.so.1.1, libcrypto.so.1.1, libc, ld-linux, librt — and no libstdc++. readelf --dyn-syms shows zero GLIBCXX/CXXABI version requirements. The C++ runtime is statically linked libc++ 18.1.

No steam_appid.txt handling in the binary. A string search for steam_appid / SteamAppId / 1086940 returned zero hits; the AppID appears only as the immediate `mov edi,0x1095dc` fed to SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary.

Runtime signature scanning is a poor primary strategy on this binary. A 12-byte masked pattern taken from real code cost 110 ms naive / 40 ms memmem-accelerated over the 90.1 MB .text, and produced 24 matches rather than 1. Uniqueness cannot be assumed at this code size.

bg3q.py's `to` subcommand does not handle section-relative addends and silently returns wrong results for anonymous targets (it reported 116,707 references for SDL_PollEvent, which actually has exactly one PLT32 call site). The addend formula `target - 4 - 0x218be00` against dst=151262 works and I validated it against a brute-force byte scan — the tool should be fixed before anyone leans on `to` for hook-target discovery.
